red_tests.failure_fingerprint: 3 failed, 34 passed: test_every_commit_sharing_a_key_is_validated observed 1 gate check for a 3-commit KAN-180 range because SEEN_KEYS deduplicates by issue key instead of per commit; test_new_branch_with_nothing_new_does_not_walk_history observed the hook validate a commit that was not being pushed because the empty new-branch rev-list degraded to RANGE="$local_sha" and git rev-list then walked the entire history

correction_reason: The KAN-180 manifest bound this test file at sha256 af5a9ca1a2304554a654c8c567138cb2a2549f9ed88de7d3d553d4d8927c8a4a, which no longer matches the file after adding coverage for two defects found by adversarial review of the shipped hook: per-commit dedup correctness and the new-branch rev-list range. This manifest supersedes that baseline and rebinds the current test file contents.
rationale: Two defects in .githooks/pre-push, both proven by executing the real hook with bash inside a throwaway git repository and asserting on observed exit codes and output, never on the hook body alone. Defect D1 (per-commit dedup): the hook seeds SEEN_KEYS with a single space and appends "${ISSUE_KEY} ", so it deduplicates gate invocations by issue key. A range of three commits sharing KAN-180 therefore produces exactly one 'Checking TDD governance' line, which contradicts the hook's own documented contract (C), its per-commit log line, and the assertion in the header comment that it validates every commit in the pushed range. Deduplication is also unsound as a correctness device rather than merely under-reporting: the gate's verdict is a function of the worktree (manifest glob plus suite result), not of the commit under test, so having already seen a key is no evidence that a later commit sharing that key was validated. test_every_commit_sharing_a_key_is_validated pins one check per commit; test_every_distinct_key_in_a_multi_key_range_is_validated pins that a three-ticket range still yields three checks and blocks when no manifest exists. Defect D2 (new-branch range): for a branch with no existing remote ref the hook computes RANGE=$(git rev-list "$local_sha" --not --remotes). When every commit is already published to some remote that list is EMPTY, and the old fallback RANGE="$local_sha" then made git rev-list walk the entire history, silently validating commits that are not part of the push and blocking the push on pre-existing commits. test_new_branch_with_nothing_new_does_not_walk_history publishes the sandbox main to a real bare remote outside the worktree, branches from it, and asserts the hook checks nothing when nothing new is being pushed; test_new_branch_validates_the_unpublished_commits_only pins that a genuinely new branch still validates its own unpublished commits and blocks without a manifest, so the fix cannot be a blanket skip.
